mainTopic: How רבי יהודה reads the extra words about סמיכה and תמורה, and who the word 'הכל' adds in a series of rulings about מצוות
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבי יהודה's view that an heir does not do סמיכה or תמורה. The גמרא shows how he reads the three mentions of 'קרבנו'. It also shows that he uses 'המר ימיר' to include a woman in תמורה, while the רבנן learn the woman from the extra 'ו' in 'ואם'. Then the גמרא goes through a list of rulings that begin with 'הכל' (everyone) and asks who that word adds. For סוכה, לולב, ציצית and תפילין, it adds a קטן who is ready for that מצוה. For ראייה, it adds a person who is half slave and half free. Since רבינא exempts that person, the גמרא offers two other ways to explain the word: either it adds someone blind in one eye, against רבי יהודה, or the two rulings come from an earlier and a later version of a משנה, after בית הלל accepted בית שמאי's view. For שופר, 'הכל' adds a child who has reached חינוך. The amud ends as the גמרא begins the same question about the מגילה, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: How רבי יהודה uses the three mentions of 'his offering'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns 'not a גוי' and 'not someone else's offering' from one mention of קרבנו. That leaves two mentions free: one excludes a father's offering, and one includes all partners in סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The exclusion of a גוי and the exclusion of another person's offering both come from one verse. That leaves two extra: one teaches 'his offering' and not his father's offering, and the other includes all the partners of an offering in סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה can learn everything the רבנן learn from 'קרבנו' and still have one mention left over to exclude an heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן use the three mentions of 'קרבנו' for three different teachings. רבי יהודה combines two of those teachings, the גוי and the other person's offering, into one mention. This frees up a mention for his own view that an heir does not do סמיכה on an offering he inherited from his father.

keyTerms.meaning: His offering. The word repeated in the פסוקים about סמיכה.
Leaning one's hands on the animal before it is brought as a קרבן.
Partners, people who own an offering together.
To include. A word in the פסוק adds a case to the law.
They are left over, extra and free to teach something new.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, one 'קרבנו' covers both the גוי and another person's offering. The freed-up mention teaches that an heir does not do סמיכה.

phrases.english: A gentile and his fellow are derived from one verse,
phrases.notes: 'His fellow' means someone else's offering. You can't do סמיכה on a קרבן that belongs to another person.

phrases.english: two are left over for him:
one: 'his offering,' and not his father's offering,
phrases.notes: This is the heir. He inherited the animal from his father, so he does not do סמיכה on it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִידָּךְ לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל בַּעֲלֵי חוֹבְרִין לִסְמִיכָה.
phrases.english: and the other is to include all partners in placing hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier discussion of how רבי יהודה reads the three mentions of 'קרבנו'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recounting the derivations so that one mention is freed up
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every mention of 'קרבנו' is already used up, so there is no source left to exclude the heir.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה combines two exclusions into one mention, which frees one 'קרבנו' to exclude a father's offering.

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה do with 'המר ימיר'?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use the double phrase 'המר ימיר' to include an heir in תמורה. רבי יהודה does not include an heir, so what does he learn from the double phrase?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה, what does he do with this 'המר ימיר'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה learns from the double wording 'המר ימיר', since he does not use it for an heir. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every extra word in the תורה is expected to teach something. The רבנן used the double phrase to teach that an heir can do תמורה. רבי יהודה disagrees with that teaching, so the גמרא wants to know what the extra wording means for him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He shall surely substitute.' A doubled verb in the פסוק about תמורה.
Trying to switch a holy animal for another animal. Both animals become holy.
What does he do with it? What does he learn from this word?

phrases.english: And רבי יהודה, this 'he shall surely substitute,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10. The רבנן learned from this double phrase that an heir can do תמורה.

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הַאי ״הָמֵר יָמִיר״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After dealing with 'קרבנו' and סמיכה, the גמרא turns to the parallel question about תמורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יהודה learns from the doubled 'המר ימיר', since he does not use it to include an heir.

steps.title: It includes a woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה needs 'המר ימיר' to teach that a woman can also do תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to include a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה uses the double phrase to teach that a woman can do תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double phrase does not go to waste for רבי יהודה. He uses it for a different addition: a woman instead of an heir.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it, meaning he uses this word for a different teaching.
A woman.

phrases.english: He needs it to include a woman,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי יהודה, 'המר ימיר' includes a woman in the law of תמורה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that 'המר ימיר' includes a woman
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the whole section on תמורה is written in the masculine. The words 'ואם המר ימיר' are what include a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Since the whole section speaks only in the masculine, why do we end up including a woman? The verse says 'And if he shall surely substitute.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its answer. The ברייתא shows that a woman's ability to do תמורה is learned from this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a special source, we might think only men can do תמורה, because the תורה uses only the masculine form. The ברייתא points to 'ואם המר ימיר' as the extra wording that includes a woman. רבי יהודה reads this as coming from the doubled verb.

keyTerms.meaning: Masculine form, wording that speaks about a man.
Why do we end up? What makes us conclude in the end?
The verse teaches. This introduces the פסוק that is the source.
The section or topic in the תורה.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Since the whole section
speaks only in the masculine form,
why do we end up including a woman?
The verse says: 'And if he shall surely substitute.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: לְפִי שֶׁכׇּל הָעִנְיָן אֵינוֹ מְדַבֵּר אֶלָּא בִּלְשׁוֹן זָכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ברייתא as the source for the answer in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman can do תמורה, learned from the wording 'ואם המר ימיר'.

steps.title: Where do the רבנן learn a woman from?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן used 'המר ימיר' for the heir, so where do they learn that a woman can do תמורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around: if the רבנן use the double phrase for the heir, what is their source for a woman? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that a woman can do תמורה. The רבנן already used 'המר ימיר' for something else, so they must have a different source for the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion that disagrees with רבי יהודה here.

phrases.english: And the רבנן?
phrases.notes: He means: where do they learn that a woman can do תמורה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the mirror question for the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן's source is for including a woman in תמורה.

steps.title: From the extra 'and' in 'ואם'
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn the woman from the extra 'ו' of 'ואם'. רבי יהודה does not learn anything from 'ואם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From 'and if.' And רבי יהודה does not expound 'and if.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן include a woman from the extra 'ו' in 'ואם'. It adds that רבי יהודה does not learn anything from that letter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides disagree about how to read the פסוק. The רבנן learn something from the small extra letter 'ו', so the double verb is free for the heir. רבי יהודה does not treat 'ואם' as a source, so he needs the double verb for the woman and has nothing left for the heir.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if.' The extra 'ו' is read as adding a case.
He does not expound it, meaning he learns nothing from that word.

steps.whatToRemember: רבנן: 'ואם' includes a woman, and 'המר ימיר' includes an heir. רבי יהודה: 'ואם' teaches nothing, and 'המר ימיר' includes a woman, so an heir cannot do תמורה.

phrases.english: From 'and if,'
and רבי יהודה does not expound 'and if.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 and closes the discussion of רבי יהודה's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן learn a woman from 'ואם'. רבי יהודה does not expound 'ואם'.

steps.title: What does 'everyone' add for סוכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new section and asks what the word 'הכל' comes to add in 'הכל חייבין בסוכה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone is obligated in סוכה.' What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It asks what case the word 'הכל' comes to add in this ruling about סוכה, and the answer follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הכל' (everyone) suggests that someone we might have thought was exempt is included. The גמרא wants to know who that person is.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone. A word that usually comes to add an unexpected case.
What does it come to include?
The temporary hut one dwells in on סוכות.

phrases.english: 'Everyone is obligated in סוכה' —
what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section in the series of 'הכל' rulings that the גמרא is explaining.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra case the word 'הכל' includes in the obligation of סוכה.

steps.title: A child who no longer needs his mother
steps.stepSummary: 'הכל' includes a קטן who does not need his mother. The גמרא proves this from a משנה in סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It includes a minor who does not need his mother, as we learned: a minor who does not need his mother is obligated in סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'הכל' adds a young child who no longer needs his mother, and it supports this with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Children are normally not obligated in מצוות. Even so, a child old enough not to need his mother must sit in the סוכה, so the word 'הכל' comes to include him.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child who is not yet בר מצוה.
Who does not need his mother.
Obligated.

steps.confusionAlert: This child is still a קטן. He is obligated in סוכה as part of training him in מצוות, not because he has become an adult.

phrases.english: To include a minor who does not need his mother,
as we learned in a משנה: A minor who does not need his mother
is obligated in סוכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הכל' includes a קטן who does not need his mother, based on the משנה in סוכה.

steps.title: What does 'everyone' add for לולב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who is included by the word 'הכל' in 'הכל חייבין בלולב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone is obligated in לולב.' Who does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the question it asked about סוכה, now about לולב. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הכל' sounds extra, because we already know adult men must take a לולב. So the גמרא assumes 'הכל' is there to include someone we might have left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The palm branch taken on סוכות, together with the other three species
Everyone is obligated
What does it come to include?

phrases.english: 'Everyone is obligated in לולב':
what does this come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same question from Step 7, this time about לולב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is added by the word 'הכל' regarding לולב.

steps.title: It adds a child who knows how to shake the לולב
steps.stepSummary: 'הכל' includes a קטן who knows how to shake the לולב, as a משנה teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include a child who knows how to shake the לולב. As we learned in a משנה: a child who knows how to shake the לולב is obligated in לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'הכל' includes a קטן who knows how to shake the לולב, and proves it from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test for a child is tied to the מצוה itself. If he can do the shaking properly, he is old enough to be trained in לולב. This matches the pattern from סוכה, where the test was a child who does not need his mother.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child below the age of מצוות
To shake or wave the לולב

phrases.english: To include a child who knows how to shake [the לולב],
as we learned in a משנה: a child who knows how to shake
is obligated in לולב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הכל' includes a קטן who knows how to shake the לולב, based on a משנה.

steps.title: What does 'everyone' add for ציצית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who is included by 'הכל' in 'הכל חייבין בציצית'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone is obligated in ציצית.' Who does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The same question is asked again, now about ציצית. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is the same as before. 'הכל' looks extra, so it must be including someone who would not be obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: The fringes tied on the corners of a four-cornered garment

phrases.english: 'Everyone is obligated in ציצית':
what does this come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as Step 9, now about ציצית.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is added by the word 'הכל' regarding ציצית.

steps.title: It adds a child who knows how to wrap himself in a garment
steps.stepSummary: 'הכל' includes a קטן who knows how to wrap himself in a garment, as a ברייתא teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include a child who knows how to wrap himself. As a ברייתא teaches: a child who knows how to wrap himself is obligated in ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'הכל' includes a קטן who can wrap himself in a garment, and proves it from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the test matches the מצוה‎. ציצית is worn on a garment, so a child who knows how to wrap himself in one is ready for ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: To wrap oneself in a garment, like a טלית

phrases.english: To include a child who knows how to wrap himself [in a garment],
as a ברייתא teaches: a child who knows how to wrap himself
is obligated in ציצית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הכל' includes a קטן who knows how to wrap himself, based on a ברייתא.

steps.title: What does 'everyone' add for תפילין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who is included by 'הכל' in 'הכל חייבין בתפילין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone is obligated in תפילין.' Who does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The same question is asked a third time, now about תפילין. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like before, the extra word 'הכל' is assumed to include someone who would not be obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: The leather boxes with פרשיות, worn on the head and arm

phrases.english: 'Everyone is obligated in תפילין':
what does this come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as Steps 9 and 11, now about תפילין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is added by the word 'הכל' regarding תפילין.

steps.title: It adds a child who knows how to guard תפילין
steps.stepSummary: 'הכל' includes a קטן who knows how to guard the תפילין. A ברייתא teaches that his father buys him תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include a child who knows how to guard תפילין. As a ברייתא teaches: a child who knows how to guard תפילין, his father buys him תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'הכל' includes a קטן who knows how to guard תפילין properly, and brings a ברייתא as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפילין need a clean body and respect, so the test is whether the child can guard them properly. The ברייתא does not say the word 'חייב'. Instead it says his father buys him תפילין, which shows he is now part of the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: To guard the תפילין, keeping clean and treating them with respect while wearing them
His father buys for him

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the wording is different here. The ברייתא does not say 'חייב בתפילין'. It says the father buys him תפילין. That is how it shows the child is included.

phrases.english: To include a child who knows how to guard תפילין,
phrases.notes: 'Guard' here means keeping himself clean and treating the תפילין with respect while wearing them.

phrases.english: as a ברייתא teaches: a child who knows how to guard תפילין,
his father buys him תפילין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הכל' includes a קטן who can guard תפילין, and his father buys him תפילין, based on a ברייתא.
steps.whatToRemember: For סוכה, לולב, ציצית and תפילין, 'הכל' always includes a קטן who is ready for that specific מצוה. Each מצוה has its own test of readiness.

steps.title: What does 'everyone' add for ראייה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who is included by 'הכל' in 'הכל חייבין בראייה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone is obligated in ראייה.' Who does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question about ראייה, the מצוה to appear in the בית המקדש on the רגלים. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This statement comes from a different source than the earlier ones, a משנה in חגיגה. The question is the same: who does the extra word 'הכל' add?

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה to appear in the בית המקדש on the three רגלים

phrases.english: 'Everyone is obligated in appearing [at the בית המקדש]':
what does this come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same question to a new מצוה‎, ראייה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is added by the word 'הכל' regarding ראייה.

steps.title: It adds a person who is half slave and half free
steps.stepSummary: 'הכל' in ראייה includes someone who is חציו עבד וחציו בן חורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include someone who is half slave and half free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for ראייה, 'הכל' includes a person who is half slave and half free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer changes here. It is not about a child at all. It is about a person whose status is mixed, partly a slave and partly free, and 'הכל' tells us he is included in ראייה.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is half a slave and half free, for example when one of two owners freed him
A free person

steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect a קטן here like in the earlier answers. For ראייה, the person included is someone who is half slave and half free.

phrases.english: To include one who is half a slave
and half a free man.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הכל' in ראייה includes a person who is half slave and half free.

steps.title: According to רבינא, 'הכל' includes a lame man who was healed on the second day
steps.stepSummary: רבינא holds that one who is חציו עבד וחציו בן חורין is exempt from ראייה. So 'הכל' must include someone else: a חיגר on the first day of the festival who was healed on the second day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבינא, who said that a person who is half slave and half free is exempt from appearing in the בית המקדש, 'everyone' comes to include a man who was lame on the first day and healed on the second day.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer in step 16 does not work for רבינא, who exempts the half-slave. So the גמרא gives a different person whom 'הכל' includes in his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16, 'הכל' included the half-slave. רבינא says the half-slave is exempt, so he needs a different case. The new case is a person who was exempt on the first day because he was lame, and became fit to go on the second day. 'הכל' teaches that he is still obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: To include. This is the word the גמרא uses when it asks what extra case a general word adds.
A lame person, who is exempt from going up to appear in the בית המקדש
Was healed. Literally, his leg straightened out.
The מצוה to appear in the בית המקדש on the three רגלים

phrases.english: And according to Ravina, who said:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
phrases.english: one who is half slave and half free
is exempt from appearing [in the Temple],
it comes to include one who was lame on the first day
phrases.notes: 'It' means the word 'הכל' (everyone) in 'הכל חייבין בראייה.'

phrases.english: and was healed on the second day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question in step 15, because the answer in step 16 does not fit רבינא's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'הכל' add in the law of ראייה, according to רבינא?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חיגר on the first day who was healed on the second day is still obligated.

steps.title: That answer only works if every festival day is its own full obligation
steps.stepSummary: The lame-man answer works for the view that all the festival days make up for one another. But for the view that the other days only make up for the first day, a person who was exempt on the first day stays exempt. So what would 'הכל' add?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says that all the days make up for one another. But for the one who says that all the days only make up for the first day, what does 'everyone' come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 17. It shows that the answer depends on a disagreement about how the festival days work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view says each day of the festival is a full day of obligation, so someone who becomes fit on day two is now obligated. The other view says the real obligation is only on day one, and the later days are just a chance to make it up. In that view, someone who was exempt on day one was never obligated, so there is nothing for him to make up.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well. The גמרא is about to say it does not work according to another view.
Making up. A later day fills in for a missed obligation.
All the days make up for one another. Every day is a full day of obligation.
All the days make up only for the first day. The main obligation is on day one.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the person here just forgot to come on day one. He was exempt on day one because he was lame. According to 'תשלומין לראשון,' he never had an obligation, so there is nothing for him to make up later.

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says:
all [the festival days] make up for one another,
but according to the one who says:
all [the days] only make up for the first day
what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 17 by showing it fits only one side of a disagreement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that 'הכל' includes a חיגר who was healed on the second day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the obligation belongs only to the first day, someone exempt on day one is never obligated, so this case cannot be what 'הכל' adds.

steps.title: 'הכל' includes one who is blind in one eye
steps.stepSummary: The new answer: 'הכל' includes a person blind in one eye, teaching that he is obligated. This goes against a certain תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include someone who is blind in one of his eyes, and this is not like the opinion of this תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that works for both views about the festival days. It also notes that a certain תנא disagrees, and the next step will show who he is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who is completely blind is exempt from ראייה. 'הכל' teaches that someone blind in only one eye is still obligated. This answer has nothing to do with the festival-days debate, so the problem from step 18 goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is blind in one of his eyes
And not like this תנא. The answer goes against a particular opinion.
A sage from the time of the משנה and ברייתא

phrases.english: It comes to include one who is blind in one of his eyes,
and not like this tanna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 with a case that works for both views about the festival days.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the case: a different person is what 'הכל' includes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הכל' includes a חיגר healed on the second day, which works only if every festival day is a full obligation.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הכל' includes someone blind in one eye, which works for both views but goes against רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's view: one blind in one eye is exempt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes יוחנן בן דהבאי in the name of רבי יהודה: one blind in one eye is exempt from ראייה. The word in the פסוק can be read both 'he shall see' and 'he shall be seen,' so being seen requires seeing with both eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: יוחנן בן דהבאי says in the name of רבי יהודה that one who is blind in one eye is exempt from appearing. The פסוק can be read 'he shall see' and 'he shall be seen.' Just as a person comes to see, he comes to be seen. Just as seeing is done with both eyes, so being seen is done with both eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows who the תנא from step 19 is and why he disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same letters in the פסוק can be read 'יִרְאֶה' (he will see) or 'יֵרָאֶה' (he will be seen). רבי יהודה links the two readings: whoever comes to be seen must be able to see the normal way, with both eyes. So for him, one blind in one eye is exempt, and 'הכל' cannot include that person.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He will see' and 'he will be seen.' These are two readings of the same letters in the פסוק.
To see
To be seen, meaning to appear in the בית המקדש
Just as ... so too. This is how the גמרא compares two things.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבינא, 'הכל חייבין בראייה' includes either a חיגר healed on the second day (only if every day is a full obligation) or one blind in one eye. The second answer goes against רבי יהודה, who requires sight in both eyes.

phrases.english: As it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹחָנָן בֶּן דַּהֲבַאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Yoḥanan ben Dahavai says in the name of Rabbi Yehuda:
One who is blind in one of his eyes
is exempt from appearing,
as it says: 'he shall see,' 'he shall be seen,'
phrases.notes: שמות 23:17. The same letters can be read both ways, and רבי יהודה learns from both readings.

phrases.english: in the way that he comes to see
so he comes to be seen;
just as seeing is with both his eyes,
so too being seen is with both his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, יוֹחָנָן בֶּן דַּהֲבַאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the source of the opposing תנא mentioned in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, one who is blind in one eye is exempt from ראייה, because the פסוק links being seen to seeing with both eyes.

steps.title: Going back: 'הכל' does include the half-slave, using two versions of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: 'הכל' really does include חציו עבד וחציו בן חורין. רבינא's ruling is no problem, because it follows the first version of the משנה, while 'הכל' follows the later version.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you like: 'הכל' really comes to include someone who is half-slave and half-free. As for רבינא's opinion, there is no problem. One ruling follows the first version of the משנה, and the other follows the later version.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way out. It returns to the half-slave answer and shows that רבינא's ruling does not have to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17 the half-slave answer was dropped because רבינא exempts him. Now the גמרא says the two rulings come from two stages of the law: רבינא follows the first stage, and the 'הכל' of the משנה in חגיגה follows the final stage. With this answer, the גמרא no longer needs the lame-man or blind-in-one-eye cases from Steps 17-20.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
Actually, really: going back to an earlier idea
To include, to bring in
The first, earlier version of a משנה
The later, final version of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean there are two different tractates or two separate משניות. It means one משנה whose ruling changed, because בית הלל later changed their minds.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Actually, it comes to include

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין,
phrases.english: one who is half-slave and half-free,
and what was difficult for you from רבינא
is not difficult:
here it follows the first version of the משנה,
phrases.notes: רבינא's exemption fits the first version. The 'הכל' of the משנה in חגיגה fits the later version, as the next lines show.

phrases.english: there it follows the later version of the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer instead of the 'blind in one eye' answer from Steps 19-20. It goes back to the half-slave answer from Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the rulings by time: earlier version versus later version of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבינא's exemption of the half-slave seemed to rule out reading 'הכל' as including him.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבינא follows the first version, and 'הכל' follows the later version, so both can stand.

steps.title: The first version: בית הלל say the half-slave splits his days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. בית הלל rule that a half-slave works one day for his master and one day for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: someone who is half-slave and half-free works for his master one day and for himself one day. These are the words of בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the 'first version.' According to בית הלל, the half-slave simply stays half-slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view, nothing pushes the master to free him, so he stays half-slave for good. That is why רבינא, following this version, exempts him from ראייה.

keyTerms.meaning: Works for, serves his master
One day

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין,
phrases.english: One who is half-slave and half-free
serves his master one day,
and himself one day,
these are the words of בית הלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the 'first version of the משנה' mentioned in Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That there was an earlier version of the ruling in which the half-slave stays half-slave
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (also found in פסחים 88a), giving the view of בית הלל

steps.title: בית שמאי object: the half-slave cannot marry anyone
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי argue that בית הלל's plan helps the master but leaves the half-slave unable to marry. The world was created to be filled with people.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: You fixed things for his master, but not for him! He cannot marry a maidservant, and he cannot marry a free woman. Should he just never marry? But the world was created only for having children, as it says: 'He did not create it to be empty; He formed it to be lived in!'
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the משנה, בית שמאי challenge בית הלל's ruling. They show that it leaves the half-slave stuck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His free half cannot marry a שפחה, and his slave half cannot marry a בת חורין, so he has no one he is allowed to marry. Leaving him unmarried goes against פריה ורביה, which the פסוק shows is the purpose of the world.

keyTerms.meaning: You have fixed, arranged things well
A non-Jewish maidservant
A free woman
Should he stay idle, here meaning never marry
Having children, filling the world

phrases.english: בית שמאי said to them:
You have fixed things for his master,
but for himself you have not fixed things?
He cannot marry a maidservant,
he cannot marry a free woman,
should he stay idle?
But wasn't the world created
only for having children,
as it says:
'He did not create it to be empty; He formed it to be lived in!'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: תִּיקַּנְתֶּם אֶת רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted משנה. בית שמאי attack בית הלל's ruling from Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's ruling that the half-slave simply splits his days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That arrangement leaves him with no one he is allowed to marry, which goes against פריה ורביה, the purpose of creation (ישעיהו 45:18).

steps.title: The later version: the master is forced to free him, and בית הלל agree
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי's solution is that the master is forced to free the half-slave, who writes a note for half his value. בית הלל changed their minds and accepted this. This is the 'later version.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, to improve the world, we force his master to free him, and he writes a document promising half his value. And בית הלל went back and ruled like בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי give their solution, and בית הלל accept it. This is the 'later version' of the משנה, and the 'הכל' of the משנה in חגיגה follows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the final ruling, the half-slave does not stay half-slave, because the court forces his release. So the משנה in חגיגה can count him as obligated in ראייה. רבינא's exemption fits only the first version, where he stays half-slave.

keyTerms.meaning: For the betterment of the world
We force (the court forces)
A written note for half his value
And they retracted, changed their minds

steps.whatToRemember: Two stages: first, בית הלל say the half-slave just splits his days, and רבינא's exemption fits this. Later, everyone agrees the master is forced to free him, and the 'הכל' of the משנה in חגיגה, which includes him, fits this.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the rare cases where בית הלל accept בית שמאי's view. It also shows how the גמרא settles two rulings that seem to clash: they come from different stages of the law.

phrases.english: Rather, for the betterment of the world,
they force his master
and he makes him a free man,
and he writes a document for half his value,
phrases.notes: The freed slave writes it, promising to pay his master the value of his slave half later.

phrases.english: And בית הלל went back
to rule like the words of בית שמאי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִפְּנֵי תִּיקּוּן הָעוֹלָם, כּוֹפִין אֶת רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית שמאי's solution to the problem raised in Step 23 and records that בית הלל accepted it. This completes the proof for Step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The final ruling, the 'later version,' forces the master to free the half-slave. The 'הכל' of the משנה in חגיגה follows this ruling, while רבינא follows the first version, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: What does 'everyone' add for blowing the שופר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'הכל חייבין בתקיעת שופר' and asks who the word 'הכל' comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone is obligated to blow the שופר.' Who is this meant to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new 'הכל' statement, this time about שופר. It asks who the extra word 'everyone' is coming to include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like it did with 'הכל חייבין בראייה', the גמרא assumes the word 'הכל' is not extra for nothing. It must be adding some person we would otherwise have left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone; the גמרא treats this word as coming to include someone extra
What does it come to include?
Blowing the shofar on ראש השנה

phrases.english: "Everyone is obligated in blowing the shofar"
what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of 'הכל' in ראייה, the גמרא applies the same question to a new 'הכל' statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which person the word 'הכל' adds to the obligation of תקיעת שופר.

steps.title: It includes a child old enough for training
steps.stepSummary: 'הכל' comes to include a קטן who has reached the age of חינוך.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include a child who has reached the age of training in מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: 'everyone' includes a child who is old enough to be trained in מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child is normally not obligated in מצוות at all. But once he is old enough to understand the מצוה, he is trained to do it, and that is the 'obligation' the word 'הכל' is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child under the age of מצוות
Reached the age of training, old enough to be taught to do a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the child has a full תורה obligation like an adult. 'Obligated' here means he is included because of חינוך, training.

phrases.english: It comes to include a minor who has reached the age of training

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הכל' includes a קטן who has reached חינוך.

steps.title: Support: we don't stop children from blowing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה that says we do not stop a child from blowing the שופר on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: we do not stop a child from blowing the שופר on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with a משנה showing that children are allowed to blow the שופר on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing the שופר on יום טוב is normally not done without a reason. The משנה lets children blow anyway, which shows they are being trained in the מצוה, so it makes sense that 'הכל' includes them.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not hold back or stop
The holiday, here ראש השנה
To blow the shofar

steps.whatToRemember: For שופר, 'הכל' adds a child who has reached חינוך, and the support is the משנה that we don't stop children from blowing on יום טוב.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: we do not stop a minor
from blowing the shofar on the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source from a משנה for the answer in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: That a קטן who reached חינוך is included in the מצוה of שופר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in ראש השנה: אין מעכבין את הקטן מלתקוע ביום טוב.

steps.title: What does 'everyone' add for reading the מגילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes two 'הכל' statements about the מגילה and begins to explain who they include.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone is obligated in reading the מגילה' and 'Everyone is fit to read the מגילה': these come to include...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next 'הכל' question, now about reading the מגילה. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two statements are quoted together: one about who must hear the מגילה, and one about who may read it for others. The גמרא is about to say who the word 'הכל' adds in both.

keyTerms.meaning: Reading the מגילת אסתר on פורים
Fit or valid to do something, here to read for others
Obligated

phrases.english: "Everyone is obligated in reading the Megillah,"
"Everyone is fit to read the Megillah" — these come to include

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing שופר, the גמרא applies the same 'הכל' question to the מגילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which person the word 'הכל' adds in the rules of reading the מגילה.
